# @weight 1

busybox's cpio (archival/cpio.c, libarchive's get_header_cpio and
data_extract_all).  Every expectation is busybox's own output, from a busybox
built from its source, run as an ordinary user, less the banner line its usage
text starts with.  A `|` marks the end of each line written to standard
output; output that is not text is shown as its bytes in hex, 32 to a line;
`after:` is what a command run after shows.  A verbose listing's time is
shown as TIME, since it is the timezone's.

## the fixtures

### the files, which busybox made, and a run of cpio in a fresh directory

`d/` holds two files, a directory, an empty directory, a symbolic link and a
hard link, all dated 2020-01-02 03:04:05 UTC.  `a.cpio` is busybox's newc
archive of it, as root's and with the inodes renumbered, `crc.cpio` the same
as crc; `links.cpio` holds a name with a leading /, a link to an absolute
target and one through `..`.  `notcpio` and `text` are text, the second
longer than a header; `damaged.cpio` has a field that is not hex, and
`short.cpio` is cut short.  Each run is in `/tmp/x-cu-cpio/w`, made
afresh from them: PRE runs before cpio, with standard input the file IN (`-`
for none), and POST after it, both through the shell.

```cu
(do (proc-run (list "/bin/sh" "-c" "rm -rf /tmp/x-cu-cpio && mkdir -p /tmp/x-cu-cpio/w")) (def cp-f (fn (_ n) (string-append "/tmp/x-cu-cpio/" n))) (file-write-all (cp-f "fx.b64") "") (proc-run (list "/bin/sh" "-c" "cd /tmp/x-cu-cpio && base64 -d < fx.b64 > fx.tar")) (def cp-home (Sys getcwd)) (def cp-sh (fn (_ cmd out) (proc-run (list "/bin/sh" "-c" (string-concat (list "cd /tmp/x-cu-cpio/w && { " cmd "; } > " out " 2>&1")))))) (def cp-in (fn (_ name) (if (string=? name "-") "" (let ((fd (file-open-read (string-append "/tmp/x-cu-cpio/w/" name))) (buf (%str-make-raw 65536))) (let ((n (File read fd buf 65536))) (do (file-close fd) (pair buf n))))))) (def cp-norm (fn (_ f) (do (proc-run (list "/bin/sh" "-c" (string-concat (list "sed -E 's#[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2} [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}#TIME#' " f " > " f ".n")))) (file-read-all (string-append f ".n"))))) (def cp-shown (fn (_ mode) (if (string=? mode "x") (do (proc-run (list "/bin/sh" "-c" "od -An -v -tx1 /tmp/x-cu-cpio/o | tr -d ' \\n' | fold -w 64 > /tmp/x-cu-cpio/hex; echo >> /tmp/x-cu-cpio/hex")) (file-read-all (cp-f "hex"))) (Str8 replace "\n" "|\n" (cp-norm (cp-f "o")))))) (def cp-case (fn (_ fresh in pre post mode argv) (do (if fresh (cp-sh "cd /tmp/x-cu-cpio && rm -rf w && mkdir w && cd w && tar xf ../fx.tar" "/dev/null") ()) (if (string=? pre "@") () (cp-sh pre "/dev/null")) (def cp-stdin (cp-in in)) (Sys chdir "/tmp/x-cu-cpio/w") (sys-dup2 1 9) (sys-dup2 2 8) (def st (let ((oo (file-open-write (cp-f "o"))) (ee (file-open-write (cp-f "e")))) (do (sys-dup2 oo 1) (sys-dup2 ee 2) (def rs (cu-run argv cp-stdin)) (sys-dup2 9 1) (sys-dup2 8 2) (file-close oo) (file-close ee) rs))) (Sys chdir cp-home) (display (string-concat (list (cp-shown mode) "stderr:\n" (file-read-all (cp-f "e")) "status " (%cu-int->str st) "\n" (if (string=? post "@") "" (do (cp-sh post (cp-f "p")) (string-append "after:\n" (file-read-all (cp-f "p"))))))))))) (display "made"))
```
---
    made

## listing

### -t lists the members, -v as ls -l does, and the archive's blocks are said on stderr; --quiet keeps them back; a member under a hard link's other name is not listed

```cu
(do (cp-case #t "a.cpio" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-t")) (cp-case #t "a.cpio" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-tv")) (cp-case #t "a.cpio" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "--list" "--quiet")))
```
---
```output
d|
d/e|
d/link|
d/sub|
d/sub/b.txt|
d/a.txt|
stderr:
2 blocks
status 0
drwxr-xr-x 0/0         0 TIME d|
drwxr-xr-x 0/0         0 TIME d/e|
lrwxrwxrwx 0/0         0 TIME d/link -> a.txt|
drwxr-xr-x 0/0         0 TIME d/sub|
-rw-r----- 0/0         4 TIME d/sub/b.txt|
-rw-r--r-- 0/0         6 TIME d/a.txt|
stderr:
2 blocks
status 0
d|
d/e|
d/link|
d/sub|
d/sub/b.txt|
d/a.txt|
stderr:
status 0
```

### names choose members, each a glob a / matches; -F reads the archive from a file

```cu
(do (cp-case #t "-" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-t" "-F" "a.cpio" "d/sub/*")) (cp-case #t "a.cpio" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-t" "d/s*" "d/a.txt" "nope")))
```
---
```output
d/sub/b.txt|
stderr:
2 blocks
status 0
d/sub|
d/sub/b.txt|
d/a.txt|
stderr:
2 blocks
status 0
```

### -R stands in for the archive's owner; a user that is not there is said

```cu
(do (cp-case #t "a.cpio" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-tv" "-R" "5:6")) (cp-case #t "a.cpio" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-t" "-R" "nosuchuser")))
```

```output
-rw-r--r-- 5/6         6 TIME d/a.txt|
```

### what is not a newc archive: nothing, too little, another magic, fields that are not hex, an archive cut short; -F a file that is not there

```cu
(do (cp-case #t "-" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-t")) (cp-case #t "notcpio" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-t")) (cp-case #t "text" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-t")) (cp-case #t "damaged.cpio" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-t")) (cp-case #t "short.cpio" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-t")) (cp-case #t "-" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-t" "-F" "nope")))
```

## extracting

### -i makes the members, the hard link once the rest are made, each with its mode but the time it is made

```cu
(cp-case #t "a.cpio" "rm -rf d; touch -t 202101010000 ref" "find d | sort; cat d/hard d/sub/b.txt; ls -l d/link | sed 's/.* d/d/'; ls -l d/a.txt d/sub/b.txt | cut -c1-12; test d/a.txt -nt ref && echo now || echo then" "-" (list "cpio" "-i"))
```
---
```output
stderr:
2 blocks
status 0
after:
d
d/a.txt
d/e
d/hard
d/link
d/sub
d/sub/b.txt
hello
bee
d/link -> a.txt
-rw-r--r--  
-rw-r-----  
now
```

### -m gives each its time; -v names each once it is made

```cu
(cp-case #t "a.cpio" "rm -rf d; touch -t 202101010000 ref" "test d/a.txt -nt ref && echo now || echo then" "-" (list "cpio" "-imv"))
```
---
```output
d|
d/e|
d/link|
d/sub|
d/sub/b.txt|
d/a.txt|
stderr:
2 blocks
status 0
after:
then
```

### a member is not made over a file as new as it, which is said, a directory not; an older one is replaced; -u replaces it

```cu
(do (cp-case #t "a.cpio" "@" "cat d/a.txt" "-" (list "cpio" "-i")) (cp-case #t "a.cpio" "rm -rf d; mkdir -p d/sub; echo old > d/a.txt; touch -t 201001010000 d/a.txt" "cat d/a.txt" "-" (list "cpio" "-id")) (cp-case #t "a.cpio" "echo new > d/a.txt" "cat d/a.txt d/hard" "-" (list "cpio" "-iu")))
```

```cu
(do (cp-case #t "a.cpio" "rm -rf d" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-i" "d/sub/b.txt")) (cp-case #t "a.cpio" "rm -rf d" "find d | sort" "-" (list "cpio" "-id" "d/sub/b.txt" "d/hard")))
```

### a leading / is taken off, and links to an absolute target or through .. are made once the rest are

```cu
(cp-case #t "links.cpio" "@" "find tmp | sort; ls -l abs rel | sed 's/.* abs/abs/; s/.* rel/rel/'" "-" (list "cpio" "-id"))
```

### --to-stdout writes the files' contents, the names under -v to stderr

```cu
(do (cp-case #t "a.cpio" "rm -rf d" "test -e d && echo made || echo none" "-" (list "cpio" "-i" "--to-stdout")) (cp-case #t "a.cpio" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-iv" "--to-stdout" "d/a.txt")))
```

```output
hello|
```

### leading ./ and empty lines are passed over; -0 reads names ended by NUL; -F writes the archive to a file

```cu
(do (cp-case #t "names" "printf './d/sub/b.txt\\n\\n.//./d/e\\n' > names" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-o" "-H" "newc" "-F" "new.cpio")) (cp-case #f "new.cpio" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-t")) (cp-case #t "names" "printf 'd/sub/b.txt\\000d/link' > names" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-o" "-0" "-H" "newc" "-F" "new.cpio")) (cp-case #f "new.cpio" "@" "@" "-" (list "cpio" "-t")))
```

```cu
(do (cp-case #t "names" "find d | sort > names; mkdir out" "find out | sort; cat out/d/hard" "-" (list "cpio" "-p" "out")) (cp-case #t "names" "find d | sort > names" "find out | sort; test out/x/y/d/a.txt -nt d/a.txt && echo newer || echo same" "-" (list "cpio" "-pdm" "out/x/y")))
```
